title: Wöhler's Urea and the End of Vital Force
summary: Chemists once believed only living things could make organic compounds. In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler heated an inorganic salt and made urea.

notes.title: 01 – Wöhler's Urea and the End of Vital Force

keyPoints: The **vital force theory** said organic compounds needed a special power found only in living things. Berzelius supported it.
In **1828**, Friedrich Wöhler heated **ammonium cyanate**, an inorganic salt, and obtained **urea**.
NH₄CNO → NH₂CONH₂: the **same atoms** in a new arrangement.
**Kolbe** made acetic acid (1845) and **Berthelot** made methane (1856).
The vital force idea faded gradually, and modern organic chemistry began.

quiz.q: The vital force theory said organic compounds:
options: could only be made by living things
quiz.explain: It claimed a special power of life was needed.
